intent: Side panel on a native <dialog>: full-height glass surface anchored to the inline-end edge (inline-start with .drawer-start), sliding in over a blanket backdrop. Use for issue detail panes, filter panels, and secondary workflows that keep page context visible. Open it declaratively with <button commandfor="id" command="show-modal"> — the native dialog invoker — and close with command="close" or a <form method="dialog">; no JavaScript involved.

structure.description: Top strip: .drawer-title (h600 scale) plus a .drawer-close icon button, space-between.
The scrolling content region (flex: 1, overflow-y: auto, 24px inline padding).
Bottom action row, end-aligned with 8px gap. Usually a <form method="dialog"> so buttons close the drawer natively.
Icon-only close button in the header (.btn .btn-subtle .btn-icon). Wire it with commandfor + command="close" pointing at the drawer's id.

aria.when: The drawer has a visible .drawer-title — point aria-labelledby at its id; otherwise label the dialog directly with aria-label.

allowedIn: directly under <body> (the dialog renders in the top layer regardless of DOM position)

a11yNotes: The native <dialog> supplies focus trapping, Esc-to-close, and top-layer stacking — never re-implement them. Give the dialog an accessible name (aria-labelledby → .drawer-title id, or aria-label). .drawer-close is icon-only and must carry aria-label. The drawer is a glass surface: never nest another glass modal surface (dialog.modal, .flag, another .drawer) inside it. Dropdown menus inside a drawer are legitimate and supported, but note the glass-layering caveat — a glass menu over a glass drawer compounds blur, so keep menus small and prefer solid-surface content behind them. Entrance slide uses motion tokens and is collapsed by the framework-wide prefers-reduced-motion rule.
